newsitem.title: USA: No ruling in FDA-tobacco case until April 21-court.
newsitem.headline: No ruling in FDA-tobacco case until April 21-court.

text.p: The federal judge weighing the tobacco industry's court challenge to Food and Drug Administration curbs on selling cigarettes will not rule until April 21 or later, his office said Friday.
A telephone tape recording at the office of Federal District Court Judge William Osteen here said, "In the tobacco verus FDA cases, there will no rulings before April 21, 1997."

New FDA regulations require shops selling cigarettes to check identifications of young customers and limit the styles and types of tobacco advertising beyond a U.S. television ban put in place decades ago.
On February 10 Osteen heard arguments from tobacco-industry lawyers that the FDA had overstepped its authority and that the advertising curbs violated U.S. guarantees of free speech.
Whatever he decides, Osteen's rulings are widely expected to be appealed.
